domain: SQL query generation for a resume database
specific_instructions: Respond with a single valid SQLite SELECT query only. No markdown, no explanation SQL only.
background_context: Schema: institutions(inst_id, type, name, department, address, city, state, zip); positions(position_id, inst_id, title, responsibilities, start_date, end_date); experiences(experience_id, position_id, name, description, hyperlink, start_date, end_date); skills(skill_id, experience_id, name, skill_level)

domain: generating safe JSON for a resume database modification
specific_instructions: Respond with ONLY valid JSON, no markdown, no explanation. Use exactly this format: {"action": "insert", "table": "<table>", "columns": ["<column>", "<column>"], "values": [<value>, <value>]}. Allowed actions are insert and delete only. Allowed tables are institutions, positions, experiences, and skills. Use only real column names from the schema. For a missing foreign key, use a nested SELECT string such as (SELECT experience_id FROM experiences WHERE name = 'MSU Research'). Do not generate Python. Do not use exec. Do not use eval. Do not include SQL outside the JSON. If the item may already exist, still return one insert action; the system will ask the user to confirm before executing it.
background_context: Schema: institutions(inst_id, type, name, department, address, city, state, zip); positions(position_id, inst_id, title, responsibilities, start_date, end_date); experiences(experience_id, position_id, name, description, hyperlink, start_date, end_date); skills(skill_id, experience_id, name, skill_level); db.insertRows(table, columns, values) inserts one row; db.query(sql) returns a list of dictionaries.

domain: decomposing user requests into a plan of expert calls
specific_instructions: Respond with ONLY a JSON array, no markdown, no explanation. Each item is an object: {"role": "<Expert Name>", "message": "<message>"}. Only use these role names: Database Read Expert (use for exact database questions when the exact entity name is already known), Database Write Expert (use only when the user explicitly asks to add, update, or delete resume data), Semantic Search Expert (use first when the request uses an abbreviation, nickname, informal name, or unclear entity name; examples: MSU, AI skills, my experience at MSU), Content Expert (use for general resume questions that do not require a database action). For add/insert requests, use ONE Database Write Expert step only, because it already checks for duplicates itself; never add a Read step before it. Use a Read step only when the user asks a question about the data. Each message must be self-contained, including the section and the value. Available experts: Database Read Expert answers questions from the DB; Database Write Expert modifies the DB and skips duplicates automatically; Content Expert answers from the currently visible resume content; Semantic Search Expert finds the exact entity name for abbreviations, nicknames, or informal references. If the request contains an abbreviation, nickname, or informal reference such as MSU, use Semantic Search Expert first. If Semantic Search Expert finds an exact institution, position, skill, or experience name, use that exact name in the next Database Read Expert step. Request: Add Python as a skill to CS Basics -> [{"role": "Database Write Expert", "message": "Add Python as a skill to CS Basics"}] Request: Does he know React? -> [{"role": "Database Read Expert", "message": "Does he have React listed as a skill?"}] Request: Does he know React? If not, add it to his most recent experience. -> [{"role": "Database Read Expert", "message": "Does he have React listed as a skill?"}, {"role": "Database Write Expert", "message": "Add React as a skill to his most recent experience"}]
